lesson.title: Array Indexing Basics
lesson.summary: Explains the difference between array length and the last valid index, with examples of safe access patterns.
learning_objectives: Understand how Java array indexes start at 0.
Differentiate between array length and last valid index.
Apply safe indexing rules when reading and writing array elements.
recommended_steps: Review the meaning of array length and last index.
Trace a few example arrays by hand.
Rewrite the failing line using a safe final index.

lesson.title: Loop Boundaries and Off-by-One Errors
lesson.summary: Shows how loop conditions interact with array sizes and why one extra iteration can break a program.
learning_objectives: Recognize common off-by-one loop patterns.
Choose a correct stopping condition for array iteration.
Check loop boundaries against the valid index range.
recommended_steps: Inspect the loop start, condition, and update together.
Compare the final loop value with the array's last valid index.
Test the corrected loop with a small example array.

lesson.title: Conditions, Comparison, and Assignment
lesson.summary: Covers the difference between assigning a value and checking a condition, with beginner-friendly Java examples.
learning_objectives: Distinguish between assignment and comparison operators.
Recognize valid boolean conditions in Java.
Correct accidental assignment inside conditions.
recommended_steps: Review the purpose of =, ==, and boolean expressions.
Rewrite the condition in plain English.
Replace the operator and re-check the condition logic.

lesson.title: Comparing Strings the Right Way
lesson.summary: Explains why == compares object references while .equals() compares the actual characters of two strings.
learning_objectives: Understand that strings are objects, not primitive values.
Distinguish reference equality (==) from content equality (.equals()).
Choose the correct comparison for string values.
recommended_steps: Review what a String variable actually stores.
Compare two equal-text strings with == and with .equals().
Rewrite the failing comparison using .equals().

lesson.title: Loop Counters and Direction
lesson.summary: Shows how the loop condition and update step must work together so the counter moves toward the stopping point.
learning_objectives: Read a for-loop's start, condition, and update as one unit.
Predict whether a counter moves toward or away from the bound.
Fix loops whose update contradicts their condition.
recommended_steps: Write down the counter value for the first three iterations.
Check whether the values approach the loop bound.
Flip the update direction and trace again.

lesson.title: How return Ends a Method
lesson.summary: Explains that return immediately leaves the method, so statements placed after it can never run.
learning_objectives: Understand that return exits the method at once.
Spot statements that can never be reached.
Reorder logic so every needed statement runs before return.
recommended_steps: Trace the method line by line until the return.
Mark which lines execution can still reach.
Move or remove the unreachable statements.

lesson.title: Switch Cases and Fall-Through
lesson.summary: Covers how execution continues into the next case unless a break stops it, and when fall-through is intentional.
learning_objectives: Explain how a switch chooses its starting case.
Predict what runs when a case has no break.
Decide where break statements belong.
recommended_steps: Pick one input value and walk through the switch by hand.
Note every statement that runs before the switch ends.
Add break statements where the flow should stop.

lesson.title: Semicolons, Blocks, and What a Condition Controls
lesson.summary: Shows how a stray semicolon after if, for, or while creates an empty body so the condition controls nothing.
learning_objectives: Recognize that a lone semicolon is a complete empty statement.
Identify exactly which statement a condition controls.
Spot stray semicolons that silently change program flow.
recommended_steps: Look at the first character after the closing parenthesis.
Say out loud what the condition actually controls.
Remove the stray semicolon and re-check the block.

lesson.title: What an Assignment Actually Does
lesson.summary: Reviews how assignment copies the right-hand value into the left-hand variable, and why assigning a variable to itself changes nothing.
learning_objectives: Describe the direction of an assignment.
Spot assignments that have no effect.
Check that each assignment uses the intended source value.
recommended_steps: Read the assignment from right to left.
State what value the variable holds before and after.
Correct the side that should reference something else.

lesson.title: AND, OR, and Conditions That Are Always True
lesson.summary: Explains how && and || combine checks, and why OR-ing two different inequalities on the same variable is always true.
learning_objectives: Evaluate compound conditions with sample values.
Recognize conditions that can never be false.
Choose between && and || based on the intended meaning.
recommended_steps: Pick three sample values and evaluate each side of the condition.
Check whether any value makes the whole condition false.
Rewrite the condition with the operator that matches the intent.

lesson.title: Why Strings Never Change
lesson.summary: Shows that String methods return a brand-new string, so ignoring the returned value silently discards the result.
learning_objectives: Understand that Java strings are immutable.
Recognize when a method result is being discarded.
Assign string method results back to a variable.
recommended_steps: Print the string before and after the method call.
Find where the returned value should be stored.
Assign the result and verify the change.

lesson.title: Division, Modulo, and Zero
lesson.summary: Covers what happens when an integer is divided by zero and how to guard divisors before dividing.
learning_objectives: Explain why integer division by zero crashes a program.
Identify risky divisors in an expression.
Guard divisions with a zero check when needed.
recommended_steps: Circle the divisor in the failing expression.
Decide what value the divisor should really be.
Add a check or fix the constant before dividing.

lesson.title: Loop Start Values and First Checks
lesson.summary: Explains that a loop condition is tested before the first iteration, so a wrong starting value can skip the loop entirely.
learning_objectives: Know when a loop condition is evaluated.
Test the condition with the starting value by hand.
Match the start value and bound to the intended range.
recommended_steps: Plug the starting value into the condition.
Decide whether the body should run at least once.
Adjust the start value or bound so the range is correct.

lesson.title: Making Loops Stop
lesson.summary: Shows that a while loop only ends when something inside the body changes its condition, and how to spot loops that never can.
learning_objectives: List the variables a loop condition depends on.
Find the statement that changes each condition variable.
Fix loops whose condition can never become false.
recommended_steps: Underline every variable used in the while condition.
Search the loop body for lines that change those variables.
Add or fix the update so the loop can finish.
